messages.content: 我想在聖荷西附近的Walmart買蘋果、米飯和12罐瓶裝水。請顯示產品資訊和庫存情況。

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

The user wants to buy apples, rice, and 12 cans of bottled water at a Walmart near San Jose. They want product info and stock status. We need to call the function walmart_purchase with loc "San Jose" or maybe "San Jose, CA". The product list includes "apples", "rice", "bottled water". For bottled water, we need pack_size? They want 12 cans. So pack_size array should match product_list length. For apples and rice, no pack size needed. But pack_size array should have same length as product_list. We can set pack_size for apples and rice as null or 0? The function signature says pack_size?: number[]. It is optional. If we provide pack_size array, its length should equal product_list. But we can also omit pack_size entirely. But they want 12 cans of bottled water. So we might specify pack_size [null, null, 12] or [1,1,12]? But the function expects numbers. We could set pack_size [1,1,12]. That indicates quantity? Or pack_size refers to size of pack? The description: "Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified." So pack_size is optional. If we want to specify quantity for bottled water, we might set pack_size [1,1,12]. That seems okay.

Thus we call function with loc "San Jose" and product_list ["apples","rice","bottled water"] and pack_size [1,1,12].

We then get response with product info and stock status. We'll output that.
